findings.summary: Source job idempotency and indexes are not fully tenant/generation fenced
findings.details: The durable row lookup collapses all rows with the same organization, unit, and idempotency key before validating effectKey or pinned generations. A stale or reused idempotency key can return another job's workId instead of creating or rejecting the intended generation/effect, and some indexes omit organizationKey entirely.

findings.summary: Lifecycle and tombstone states can be bypassed by stale completion/control paths
findings.details: Accepted-effect replay returns before checking current lifecycle/emergency generations, and cancelled/revoked/superseded transitions do not require a current lease. The reclaim helper also lacks an explicit terminal-state guard, so lifecycle/tombstone safety is not enforced consistently around stale workers.

findings.summary: Lease receipt hashing leaks raw token material
findings.details: Attempt receipts persist a tokenHash that includes the raw token length and first four characters, while the lease token itself is deterministic from idempotency/effect values. This is not an opaque non-disclosing receipt and leaks token material into durable job records.

findings.summary: Claim and completion paths patch snapshot-derived state without durable CAS
findings.details: The implementation computes lease and completion transitions from an in-memory row snapshot and patches full row state. The only compare check appears after enqueueAction for workId, not before claiming or before accepting the final effect, leaving concurrent workers and stale snapshots insufficiently fenced.

findings.summary: Enqueue replay can duplicate external work before workId is persisted
findings.details: External work is enqueued before the workId is saved on sourceProcessingJobs. A crash or retry between those steps leaves a claimed row with no workId, so a replay can enqueue again even though only one accepted effect is later suppressed.

findings.summary: Revision and terminal-state fencing is not enforced atomically for all state transitions
findings.details: Pinned generation checks exist only for successful completion, while failure/control transitions can patch terminal lifecycle states without lease/generation checks. The final success patch also lacks an atomic current-row compare, so stale-generation races are not durably fenced.
